comment: The `implements` edge, pinned in both directions. `Addable` and `Both` refine `Number`; `Both` also refines `Container`. POSITIVE half: the edges exist, carry the `implements` label, and sit at the concept's own declaration line. NEGATIVE half: the analyzer must not relabel a concept refinement as `extends` (the nominal-class label), must not emit `implements` for a concept that refines nothing, and must not treat a concept's formal parameter as a read. The forbid on `extends Number` is the half that would catch a 'helpful' fix that routed the concept clause through collectInheritance, which is the neighbouring-type confusion question 4 asks about. REVISED 2026-10-04: the `of`-form's GENERIC-TARGET shape (`of Source[T]`), its QUALIFIED-TARGET shape (`of mod.Contract`, whose leading `.` parses as an ERROR node with no field) and its SELF-CYCLE shape were added after nim-lang/nimony took the family's corpus count off zero. All three occur in real code; none was pinned, because a family can be fully fixture-covered and still be unpinned on the shape most of its corpus edges use.

expectRelationships.comment: `type Addable = concept x of Number` — the `of` clause is the refinement, read off the grammar's `refines` field
`of Number, Container` is a refinement_list of two entries; this is the first
the second entry of the same refinement_list — one edge per named contract, not one per clause

the OLD-styled spelling `concept of Number`, where `of` follows `concept` with no formal parameter. The grammar makes the parameter list optional, so a reader that only looked after a parameter list would miss this form entirely

DELIBERATE co-existence, mirroring what `inherits` already does: `extends` and `references` are both published for an object base, and `implements` and `references` are both published for a concept refinement. They answer two different questions — 'which contract does this claim' versus 'which types does this depend on' — and the standing rule R9 requires the declared-type graph regardless of what the ontology edge says

THE `is` SPELLING — `type HasArea = concept x` with body `x is Shape`. doc/manual_experimental.md:1205-1213 names it as the other way to write the same fact ('When the matched type within a concept is directly tested against a different concept, we say that the outer concept is a refinement of the inner concept'). Over 4,101 corpus files the `of` clause occurs 0 times against 216 concepts, so a reader that takes only the clause reports the type absent from a corpus full of concepts

`x is Shape or name(x) is Sized` — the chain's first operand is a statement-level test of the parameter and refines; the second's left side is a CALL, so it is a constraint on a computed value and refines nothing. One guard covers both halves of an `or` chain without parsing the chain

`concept x of Source[T]` — the GENERIC-TARGET shape, 2 of the 47 corpus `implements` edges (nimony/tests/nimony/concepts/tconceptinheritnotgeneric.nim:7 `Bar = concept of Foo[T]`, tconceptinvocationbody.nim:39 `MutableIndexable*[T] = concept of Indexable[T]`). The target is the CONSTRUCTOR `Source`, not the type argument `T`. A reader that takes the last segment of the refinement list publishes `implements -> T`, a fabricated edge pointing at a generic parameter — the same confusion the `references` side records for `BlenderRgb[Rgba8]`. This lane's own oracle made exactly that mistake on its first pass and the cross-check caught it, which is why the shape is pinned on the ANALYZER side too.

forbidRelationships.comment: guard 1, the field shape: `o.length is Sized` constrains the type of the FIELD `length` and refines no contract. Corpus shape: nim/tests/concepts/texplain.nim:136 reads `o.foo is RegularConcept`, where RegularConcept IS a same-file concept — so without this row a reader that only checked the right-hand side would publish a fabricated refinement

guard 2, the concrete-type shape: `x is int` is a type constraint on the matched parameter and `int` implements nothing. MEASURED on the pinned 4,555-file corpus (validation/m14/measurements/nim/ruling-probe.json, analyzer sha256 9d9ee478e3295c28): 156 `is` expressions sit inside a concept body, 124 name an identifier on the right and 32 do not. The most common unguarded right-hand sides are T(31) int(23) bool(15) string(10) V(5) float(5) SomeFloat(4) BaseField(4) Ordinal(3) A(3) — generic parameters and builtins, so an unguarded reader fabricates 124 edges pointing at builtin types and type parameters

guard 3, the self-reference: `r is Recursive` is recursion, not refinement. The corpus shape is `distinctBase(x) is Primitive` at nim/tests/concepts/trecursive_concepts.nim:26, where the left is a CALL on the parameter so guard 4 declines it and Primitive (a same-file concept) is never read as a supertype. rightNamesSameFileConcept is 0 and passesAllGuards is 0, which is why this family's corpus edge count is 0 rather than the 7 concept-declared names the wider population contains

the chain's second operand, `name(x) is Sized`: its left side is a call on the parameter, not the parameter, so it constrains a computed value. The corpus carries this exact shape at trecursive_concepts.nim:26 (`distinctBase(x) is Primitive`)

THE FABRICATION GUARD. `Meters` is an ordinary object type, and Nim has no syntax for declaring that a type implements a concept: satisfaction is the compiler's structural match against the concept body at instantiation time. So no `implements` edge may name it. An analyzer that inferred satisfaction from the members it can see would publish one edge per (object type x concept) pair and every one would be fabricated — unresolvable at the target end, counted `unexplained` by the oracle, and wrong refactoring advice in bb_impact. This row is the one that catches it

the neighbouring-type confusion: a concept refinement is NOT the nominal class hierarchy, which `extends` already carries. A fix that routed the `of` clause through collectInheritance would satisfy every positive row above and still be wrong here
`Number` refines nothing. An `implements` edge needs a named supertype contract; a concept with no `of` clause has none, and emitting one would be a fabricated edge
the parameterless concept with no `of` clause — the same fabrication guard on the other spelling

`concept x of Number` writes its formal parameter with no symbol_declaration and no type annotation, so it is invisible to the ordinary declaration-name test. The concept is a scope frame, so the read of `x` in `useContract`'s parameter position is a read of a BINDING and must not be attributed to file scope

the type ARGUMENT is not the refined contract. `of Source[T]` refines `Source`; publishing an edge to `T` would be the fabricated edge the row above exists to catch, and `T` is a generic parameter that resolves at neither end

the SELF-CYCLE, `of`-form twin of the `Recursive` forbid: `type Cycle = concept of Cycle` is the whole body of nimony/tests/nimony/concepts/tconceptcycle.nim, whose upstream tconceptcycle.msgs reads `Error: concept inheritance cycle detected`. A concept refining itself is not a relationship, so no edge may be published at all — this is a real corpus file, and `gap-hunt`-class reasoning does not cover it because the file parses cleanly and the construct is legal syntax
